children: The Federal Trade Commission has asked a federal judge to hold in contempt the former CEO of Retrophin and Turing Pharmaceuticals (now renamed Vyera Pharmaceuticals), Martin Shkreli, for allegedly violating a 2022 court order by trading pharmaceutical industry stocks and voicing opinions about companies.

A motion filed Tuesday in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York alleges that Shkreli, who also started several venture capital firms, has traded in at least 60 pharma stocks and posted opinions on pharma companies on social media platforms, such as YouTube, X, and Reddit.

In February 2022, Shkreli was issued a lifetime ban from participating directly or indirectly in the pharmaceutical industry, including taking an ownership interest in such companies. However, the FTC alleges that shortly after his release from prison in May 2022, he began doing livestreams on YouTube.

Since July 2022, the FTC says that Shkreli has been trading in pharma stocks in four phases: a 2022 trading competition with another YouTuber; shorting a small biotech company in 2024; a 2025 trading challenge in which he shorted three small biotech companies and traded in other pharma stocks; and a trading challenge started in June 2026 with $10M involving pharma stock trading.
The agency is asking the court to force Shkreli to divest his pharma stocks, pay a fine equal to the profits he has made, and face consequences for any future violations.

Shkreli, who earned the nickname "pharma bro," gained notoriety in 2015 when, as Turing CEO, the company acquired the manufacturing license for the drug Daraprim and then proceeded to raise the price to $750 per pill from $13.50 while making agreements to make it difficult for other companies to make a version.

Shkreli was convicted in federal court in 2017 of two counts of securities fraud and one count of conspiracy. He was sentenced to seven years in prison and up to $7.4M in fines. In a separate civil case, he was fined $64.6M.

title: FTC wants Martin Shkreli held in contempt for trading pharma stocks
